text:
jen_security: quick one — after last night's KMS key rotation some decrypts from the analytics pipeline started failing with AccessDenied. throwing this into the thread so we have a single place to triage.
jen_security: error from app logs: "ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User: arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/analytics-worker/ session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01-2345"
jen_security: we rotate keys with an automated Lambda that creates a new CMK, re-wraps a new envelope key, and re-issues grants to the consumer role via GrantTokens returned by CreateGrant. The consumer assumes a cross-account role in account 222222222222.
mike_sre: do we see the grant ids in CloudTrail for CreateGrant? those should appear with granteePrincipal = the role arn in the key account.
jen_security: I pulled CT lines, CreateGrant exists and returns GrantId: "g-0a1b2c3d" in account 111111111111. But the application trying to decrypt is still getting AccessDenied.
anna_infra: did the consumer include the GrantToken in the Decrypt call? if the grant was just created it only applies if the caller sends the grant token until the grant is fully visible.
jen_security: app does not send grant token currently. it relies on IAM + key policy. we thought CreateGrant would make decrypt allowed for the role principal immediately.
alex_iam: note: CreateGrant has nuance for cross-account assumed roles. If the grantee is an assumed-role principal (arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/analytics-worker/...), you need to create the grant for the role principal arn (arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/analytics-worker), not the assumed-role session ARN. cloudtrail sometimes shows assumed-role as the grantee and that won't match key policy checks.
mike_sre: can you paste the key policy and the role trust/policy (redact IDs)? small snippet is fine.
jen_security: key policy snippet: ```json
{ "Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Sid":"AllowUse","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/analytics-worker"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":"*"} ] }
```
jen_security: role policy snippet: ```json
{ "Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01-2345"} ] }
```
anna_infra: those look OK on paper. but if the grant was created against the wrong principal shape, KMS won't honor it for an assumed session. also check whether the key got automatically re-created (new key id) and the role policy points at the old key.
jen_security: confirmed the key id in role policy matches the new CMK.
alex_iam: another angle: are we using an envelope key pattern where the application holds a ciphertext blob encrypted under the old key? After rotation the app should re-encrypt with new plaintext DEK; otherwise Decrypt will be done against the key that encrypted it (which might be scheduled for deletion). CloudTrail Decrypt events show keyId = old key sometimes.
jen_security: logs for one failed decrypt show cipherKeyId: "key/oldkey-111" and Decrypt called on new key id — maybe a mismatch. sample log line: ```[2026-01-12T03:14:22Z] decrypt failed user=arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/analytics-worker/ sess="m-..." keyId=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/oldkey-111 error=AccessDenied```
mike_sre: if ciphertext was encrypted with the old key, KMS will try to decrypt with that key. If old key has had its key policy or grants revoked/rotated away, it could deny.
jen_security: we rotated by creating a new key and re-wrapping DEKs; old key is still Enabled but we removed the role principal from the old key's key policy as part of cleanup. maybe some workers still have blobs referencing the old key and can't decrypt now.
anna_infra: yep that would explain it. either rewrap all DEKs or re-add the role as a principal on old key until rewrap completes.
alex_iam: also watch for kms:ViaService conditions in key policy — if the grantee is cross-account via KMS multi-account access, that can block assume-role sessions depending on how the trust is configured.
mike_sre: quick repro steps we can try: 1) run aws kms decrypt with --ciphertext-blob of a failing blob from the key account while passing --grant-tokens if available; 2) assume the consumer role and try decrypting directly; 3) compare CloudTrail Decrypt events for allowed vs denied.
jen_security: trying step 2 now: ```bash
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/analytics-worker --role-session-name test1 --duration-seconds 900
# use returned creds to call
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --region us-west-2
``` got same AccessDenied.
anna_infra: run that decrypt including the GrantToken returned by CreateGrant (if you still have it). CreateGrant response had GrantToken in lambda logs? you may have expired token but get GrantId from CT.
jen_security: lambda logs show CreateGrant returned GrantToken: "token-xyz". consumer client did not send it. can we inject it via the CLI? yes: ```aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --grant-tokens token-xyz``` trying...
devops-bot: scheduled-run: kms-rewrap-job started for rotation batch 2026-01-11T02:00Z
jen_security: with grant token passed the decrypt succeeded. so this proves the grant was required during the window after rotation.
mike_sre: that matches expected behavior: a newly created grant can be used via GrantToken by callers until propagation completes. if the consumers don't send the token, they must rely on IAM/key policy or the grant must be created in a way that doesn't require tokens (e.g., pre-existing grants or policy-based access).
alex_iam: operational recommendations: 1) avoid quick-remove of role from old key policy until all DEKs are rewrapped. 2) if you create grants during rotation for cross-account assumed-role sessions, either return grant tokens to the consumer (hard) or ensure the grant principal is the role ARN (not an assumed session) so normal policy checks work. 3) emit a short-lived rotation marker and stall cleanup until consumers confirm rewraps.
anna_infra: for now, re-add the analytics role to the old key policy (temporary) and schedule a full rewrap sweep + validate decrypted blobs count. That will immediately restore decrypts without requiring grant tokens.
jen_security: will re-add principal to old key policy now and kick a rewrap. also adding a small retry in the client to include grant-token if present from rotation lambda.
mike_sre: add an integration test for rotation that verifies consumers can decrypt a sample blob both during rotation and after rewrap.
jen_security: thanks all — action items pinned: re-add role temporarily, run rewrap sweep, update rotation lambda to pass grant tokens to consumer (or create grants against role ARN), add integ test. closing until sweep completes.
alex_iam: add note in runbook about not deleting key policy entries until rewrap confirmation.
jen_security: will update runbook and post results here when sweep done. :thumbsup:
